cost_reported: about $17,500 at API list prices for all experiments, including estimated exploratory runs (Table A7); visual cortex searches about $5,000
evidence_notes: WSP (writing networks from scratch) is the whole paper. Claude Code agents write Python that sets the weights, with visible-accuracy feedback each iteration (p.3-4), so code_or_tensor_tool and closed_loop; for brain encoding a fixed ridge regression is fitted on the agent's features (p.4). NLP models stay near 190,000 parameters (p.4), used as the approximate maximum. Opus 5.5 audits constraint-following (p.4), so LLM in grading is yes. Agents mostly reuse known algorithms and motifs (p.4, p.12); the fMRI jump came from story-position features that exposed a scan-timing confound (p.8). No preregistration; code at github.com/csinva/weight-space-programming-autoresearch (p.1).
